sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Montgomery County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value of every parcel, and the Sheriff's Office sends the bills and takes the payments. Deeds are recorded by the County Clerk, whose line is (859) 498-8700.

  • PVA, Montgomery County: (859) 498-8710. This is the office for assessment questions, tax roll review and exemption forms.
  • Sheriff's Office: (859) 498-8704. Mail payments to 1 Court Street, Suite 4, Mt. Sterling, KY 40353, with the bill number on the check.
  • County Clerk: (859) 498-8700, for recording the deed and for delinquent bills after they leave the sheriff.

The sheriff's page says bills and paid receipts can be viewed and printed online, but a bill cannot be paid online. A seller who wants a payoff figure should call the sheriff rather than look for a web portal.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Montgomery County for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Montgomery County sits in the Outer Bluegrass, with ground that runs from 707 to 1,447 feet above sea level and 197 square miles of land. The county was cut from Clark County in 1796, and Mount Sterling, the county seat, has held the courthouse ever since. Census Bureau figures put the 2025 population at 28,822, up 2.5% from the 2020 base.

Mount Sterling is about 34 miles east of Lexington. Interstate 64 passes through the north end of town with exits 110 and 113, and U.S. 60 and U.S. 460 cross in the center. The Census Bureau reports a mean trip to work of 25.7 minutes for county residents. The Mount Sterling area is a micropolitan area that belongs to the larger Lexington combined statistical area, according to the county's Wikipedia entry.

Montgomery County has no countywide planning and zoning. The fiscal court's FAQ says subdivisions within five miles of Mt. Sterling follow the city's zoning and subdivision rules, and the city has its own planning and zoning board. A seller with a rural lot or a split parcel should ask the city office before promising a buyer anything about subdividing.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about housing in Montgomery County?
sections.html:
The numbers below come from Census QuickFacts and describe a county where most homes are owner-occupied but renting is common. The median owner-occupied value of $172,200 is the yardstick an owner can use when judging whether an assessment looks reasonable.

  • Housing units, 2025 estimate: 12,422, with 53 building permits issued in 2025.
  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 68.3%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $172,200.
  • Median monthly owner costs: $1,242 with a mortgage and $470 without.
  • Median gross rent: $830.
  • Median household income: $56,396, with 15.5% of residents in poverty.

About 88.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Turnover is therefore modest, and a house that needs work often sits longer than a move-in-ready one.

sections.h2: When are Montgomery County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The 2026 bills went out the last week of September, and collection began October 1, 2026. Kentucky's due-date statute, KRS 134.015, sets the pattern of discount, face amount and penalties, and the sheriff posted the exact dates.

Montgomery County collection calendar for 2026 bills
DatesAmount owed
October 1 to November 1, 2026Bill less 2% discount
November 2 to December 31, 2026Face amount
January 1 to January 31, 2027Face amount plus 5%
February 1 to April 15, 2027Face amount plus 21%

The sheriff adds a warning. Payments made while a 10% penalty applies but before the bill moves to the clerk carry an extra 10% sheriff's fee. On the close of business April 15, 2027, unpaid bills pass to the County Clerk, where a 20% County Attorney fee, a 10% clerk fee and 1% monthly interest apply. The clerk may also sell a delinquent bill to a third party the following summer.

sections.h2: How much does a late Montgomery County bill cost in dollars?
sections.html:
Take a $1,500 bill. Paid by November 1 it costs $1,470. From November 2 through December it costs $1,500. In January the 5% penalty makes it $1,575, and from February 1 to April 15 the 21% period brings it to $1,815. The gap between the earliest and latest sheriff payment is $345 on a bill that size.

After April 15 the clerk's fees stack on top, so the payoff is whatever the clerk quotes on the day. If a prior-year bill is open on a house you are selling, get that number before choosing a closing date. The sheriff also asks that a mortgage company or previous owner receive any bill meant for them, so forward a bill that belongs to your lender's escrow account.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Montgomery County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA, not the clerk. Kentucky values property as of January 1, and KRS 133.120 requires a conference with the PVA or a deputy before any formal appeal. A conference can be held by telephone if you ask.

The real property tax roll is open for 13 days starting the first Monday in May under KRS 133.045, unless the state moves the dates. If the conference does not settle the value, file a written petition with the County Clerk. It must name the property, give your reasons and state what you think the fair cash value is. The deadline is one workday after the inspection period ends. The county board of assessment appeals then holds a hearing, and you carry the burden of showing evidence such as an appraisal, sales listings or construction costs.

Appealing does not pause the bill. You pay on the value you claimed, and any increase the board finds is billed later with interest. A taxpayer who skips the county board cannot go straight to the state Board of Tax Appeals.

sections.h2: Is a homestead exemption available in Montgomery County?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners who are 65 or older or who are classified as totally disabled. The Kentucky Department of Revenue sets the 2025 and 2026 exemption at $49,100, and it comes off the assessed value of the home. A house assessed at the county median of $172,200 would be taxed on $123,100.

The application goes to the Montgomery County PVA at (859) 498-8710. Proof of age can be a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claims must be renewed each year unless the owner is a veteran with a service-connected disability or has been found permanently and totally disabled by the Social Security Administration or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when a Montgomery County house sells?
sections.html:
Ownership for tax purposes is fixed on January 1, and a bill for a purchase made after that date is issued in the former owner's name. The seller therefore usually receives the bill for the year of sale. KRS 134.015 also makes each year's tax a personal debt of the owner on the assessment date.

  • Ask the sheriff whether the current bill is paid and which collection period applies.
  • Agree in the contract how the year's tax is split between seller and buyer.
  • Put the buyer's mailing address in the deed's in-care-of line for tax bills, as KRS 382.135 requires.
  • Record the deed with the County Clerk at (859) 498-8700.

A lien attaches once taxes go delinquent and can follow the property for 11 years under KRS 134.420, whoever owns it. Title companies check for it, so clear any old bill first.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Montgomery County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Sheriff's Office at (859) 498-8704 for the amount due and payment status. Call the PVA at (859) 498-8710 if you think the value is wrong.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Montgomery County property tax online?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff says bills and receipts can be viewed and printed online, but payment must be mailed or made in person at 1 Court Street, Suite 4, in Mt. Sterling. Include the bill number and a stamped envelope if you want a receipt back.

faqs.q: What is the penalty if I miss the December 31 date in Montgomery County?
faqs.a: A 5% penalty applies from January 1 through January 31, and a 21% penalty applies from February 1 through April 15. After April 15 the bill moves to the County Clerk, who adds a 20% attorney fee, a 10% clerk fee and monthly interest.
Only partly. The county has no countywide zoning, but Mt. Sterling has its own planning and zoning, and subdivisions within five miles of the city must follow its regulations.

faqs.q: How much is the Kentucky homestead exemption for Montgomery County owners?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, for owners 65 or older or totally disabled. File the application with the Montgomery County PVA.
